Topic: USD/JPY Intraday Range as an Independent Intervention Detector — Calibration Scale + the Wrong-Clock False-Negative Failure Mode
Key_Fact: Daily intraday RANGE in USD/JPY is a usable own-instrument detector for suspected MOF operations, independent of wire reporting. CALIBRATION SCALE (own repaired data, `usdjpy.py` / `workbook/USDJPY.tsv`): 2026-04-30 = 5.15y on a CONFIRMED ~¥5.48T MOF op; 2026-05-06 = 2.84y on a confirmed ~¥4.3T op; 2026-07-30 = 5.82y (suspected ~¥8.45T); 2026-07-31 = 3.73y; 2026-08-03 = 2.67y — against a 60-session PRE-EPISODE maximum of just 1.98y and a prior-year ≥2.5y frequency of 3/259 (~1.16% of sessions). ⇒ intervention days are the highest-range events in the series by a wide margin; the script's CRIT alert bar is 4.0y. 🔴 FAILURE MODE (found and fixed 2026-08-02) — A GUARD KEYED TO THE WRONG CLOCK, FAILING SILENTLY AND FALSE-NEGATIVE: `usdjpy.py`'s skip-guard derived "today" from local `datetime.now()` (Eastern) while yfinance labels USDJPY=X bars in Europe/London, so any boot after ~19:00 ET saw the next London-day's hours-old PARTIAL bar as "not today" and appended it as final; the idempotent-by-date append then made it PERMANENT and it could never self-correct. 10 of 60 sessions were truncated, EVERY ONE under-stating the range — worst case 7/30 stored as a 0.33y range against a true 5.74y, so the detector reported "normal daily range" on the largest yen move since Dec-2023. A second defect compounded it: the L3 audit checked the full 60d lookback while L2 only rewrote inside 10d, so pre-fix rows were re-flagged every run and could never heal (fixed by a `--revise-window N` backfill hatch — a flag, not a default, because widening rewrites history). ⚠️ Known remaining defect (flagged, not fixed): Yahoo's daily FX CLOSE field is a bar-boundary snapshot (Open≈Close on every row), so the script's headline LEVEL is unreliable — it printed 160.18 against a true 7/31 close of 157.40. Use the RANGE, not the level.
